decisions.onDecide: Delete the two unchosen src/lab/Direction*.tsx files and their routes in src/App.tsx, fold the winner into src/views/Homepage.tsx, and set this decision to the chosen slug.
decisions.note: 19/08: team chose C as the base for its cardless feel, and asked for A's marquee and collection look to be brought across. A and B stay published for reference; C is now the working direction. 20/08: C4 added as a fourth direction — not a variant of C but a different structure, built to the brief of keeping only the colour and the wave/loop motif.

PRODUCT.md records the guidelines ratio as 60% white / 30% violet / 10% teal; the header comment in src/index.css records it as violet 60% / white 30% / teal 10%. Direction B reads it the PRODUCT.md way (paper ground), A and C the index.css way (violet ground). Confirm against docs/BRAND-GUIDELINES-TI-COOLTURE.pdf before committing to a direction.
decisions.resolution: User confirmed: 60% violet, 30% black and white, 10% teal. Violet is the dominant ground. Direction C was retoned to match; measured across 2660 sample points over the full page: violet 52%, white 14%, ink 12%, teal 9%, photography 13% (the hero photo carries a violet multiply scrim, so perceived violet sits near 60%).

decisions.question: Should the pinned collections window run one step further so every collection gets its 60% moment?
decisions.note: The brief described the window sliding from (C1 60, C2 30, C3 10) to (Cn-2 60, Cn-1 30, Xem them 10), which is what ships. With four collections that means Collection 4 peaks at 30% and never reaches 60%. One-line change in PinnedCollections: cursorMax = panelCount - 2 instead of panelCount - 3.

wireframes.html MO-7 says the collections pin 'releases directly into the footer reveal - the two are consecutive, never simultaneous'. The team's 19/08 note puts the map strip between collections and the footer, which ships. The two are still consecutive, just with the strip between them; confirm this supersedes the wireframe note.

Direction C currently spends part of its 30% on ink grounds (the map strip, one collection panel). The brand studies deliberately leave those alone so the comparison isolates the device layer. Decide whether the ink grounds should become white to match the book.

Team feedback folded into Direction C: hero gradient runs white to violet with a dark nav material over it; collections show one lead piece with a non-wrapping name; the district map is one track driven by mouse drag, touch swipe and buttons through a single spring (src/lab/useDragTrack.ts, built to Apple's fluid-interface rules - 1:1 tracking, velocity handoff, momentum projection, rubber-banding); every change of ground is a gradient band so no abrupt transitions remain; What's in store runs one lane on mobile.

decisions.note: Every <Link viewTransition> in src/views does nothing: React Router only honours the prop under a data router, and src/App.tsx mounts <BrowserRouter> + <Routes>. Verified by patching document.startViewTransition and clicking a product card — it was never called. So the product-image continuity the SPEC asks for has never run, and the only transition that does fire is withDirectionalTransition() on a filter chip, which slides and scales the whole page (1.06 → 1) on a spring that overshoots — the jerky zoom the team reported. The lab studies drive the transition explicitly (src/lab/subpages/shared.tsx › ContinuityLink) and name only the clicked image, so exactly one pair morphs. Whichever directions are chosen, the fix belongs in src/views too.

Seed extended from 12 to 77 placeholder products across the same six shops (src/lib/mock/catalogue.ts), with shops crossing categories so filter combinations mean something, three NULL prices for the Liên hệ path, three image slots per product, and a short_desc_vi for every product including the original twelve, which had none. Publication dates use a coprime stride so "mới nhất" interleaves the shops. Still INVENTED placeholder content — it must not ship to a public demo.

decisions.question: What gives when a 16:9 hero image has to sit on a portrait phone?
decisions.note: Team 31/08: the deck's ratio on mobile does not match PC, and they asked for lab options rather than a pick. The shipped deck is 4:5 on phones, 16:10 from sm, 16:9 from lg. The constraint that forces the trade-off is already recorded in constraints.must: every shop image slot is 16:9. object-cover on a box narrower than 16:9 crops the sides, so at 4:5 a visitor sees 45% of the width the shop framed. Every figure below is measured on a 375x812 box in the study, not estimated.
